title: U.S. House · New York's 23rd District
area: Western New York, including Chautauqua, Cattaraugus, Allegany, Wyoming, Livingston, Ontario, Yates, Steuben, Schuyler and part of Erie County.

context.text: Aaron Gies defeated Kevin Stocker in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary, 70.7%-27.9%. The Republican and Conservative primaries were canceled; incumbent Nick Langworthy advanced without appearing on either ballot.

summary.text: Nick Langworthy is the Republican and Conservative incumbent, a former chairman of the New York Republican State Committee and Erie County Republican Party first elected to the House in 2022. He chairs the Rules Committee's Legislative and Budget Process Subcommittee and also serves on Oversight and Government Reform and Energy and Commerce.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree in political science and government from Niagara University in 2003.
Worked as a congressional staffer, including as district director for Rep. Chris Lee, and as president of Liberty Opinion Research.
Served as chairman of the New York Republican State Committee and the Erie County Republican Party before his election to Congress.

priorities.text: Describes his focus as protecting constitutional rights and what his campaign materials call the values that make America a strong and prosperous country.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, the Committee on Energy and Commerce (Health, Energy and Environment subcommittees), and chairs the Legislative and Budget Process Subcommittee of the Committee on Rules in the 119th Congress.

summary.text: Aaron Gies, a St. Bonaventure University theology professor, is the Democratic and Working Families Party nominee challenging incumbent Rep. Nick Langworthy in NY-23, running on affordability, universal healthcare, and rebuilding rural infrastructure.

background.text: Gies says he was raised in a working family; his father ran a small contracting business and his mother worked as a school secretary.
background.quote: I was raised in a working family. My father ran a small contracting business. My mother worked as a school secretary.

background.text: He describes his career as including work as a teacher, a nonprofit leader, and roles waiting tables, doing bookkeeping for a Main Street business, and working on a nonprofit farm.
background.quote: I've spent my life serving communities — as a teacher, nonprofit leader, and person of faith.

priorities.text: Says his central campaign message is that a good life should be affordable, citing rising costs, wages that have not kept pace, and corporations getting special treatment.
priorities.quote: A good life should not be a luxury.

priorities.text: Cites medical debt as one of the most common causes of bankruptcy and says cuts to Medicare, Medicaid, VA benefits, and rural healthcare systems threaten local hospitals and nursing homes.
priorities.quote: Medical debt is now one of the most common causes of bankruptcy in America.

priorities.text: Says he would strengthen unions and workers' bargaining power rather than give tax breaks and deregulation to large corporations.
priorities.quote: Instead of tax breaks and deregulation for large corporations, Aaron supports raising wages and strengthening workers' bargaining power.

priorities.text: Describes housing as scarce and increasingly unaffordable in Western New York and the Southern Tier and says it should be treated as a basic human need rather than only an investment.
priorities.quote: Housing is not just an investment; it is a basic human need.

positions.summary: Supports codifying Roe v. Wade's abortion protections into federal law and would oppose a national abortion ban.
positions.quote: I support codifying the protections of Roe into law and would vote no on any attempted national abortion ban.

positions.summary: Supports universal background checks and red-flag laws while also affirming Second Amendment rights.
positions.quote: I support universal background checks and red flag laws to keep guns out of the hands of those who are likely to use them to commit crimes.

positions.summary: Supports secure borders and consistent enforcement, but pairs that with due process for undocumented people and a new guest-worker program rather than enforcement alone.
positions.quote: I support strong, secure borders and fair treatment for law-abiding immigrants... Real reform should include a fair process for new entries, due process for undocumented people, a guest worker program that serves our country's economic needs, and consistent enforcement.

positions.summary: Campaigns under a "Universal Healthcare" priority, citing medical debt as a leading cause of bankruptcy and opposing cuts to Medicare, Medicaid, VA benefits, and rural healthcare systems.
positions.quote: Medical debt is now one of the most common causes of bankruptcy in America.

positions.summary: Supports renewable energy development and opposes new fracking and nuclear projects.
positions.quote: Renewable energy makes us more resilient and energy independent and I'll fight for federal dollars for these projects... I oppose irresponsible data center buildout, fracking and new nuclear projects.

researchNotes: Gies's campaign website (aaronforny23.com) blocked automated access directly; the live site was checked instead and supplied biography, priorities and positions. His Ballotpedia page still has no biography section and no completed Candidate Connection survey. A fact-check found that two claims sourced to the site could not be verified there: a "$15 minimum wage" quote (no mention of minimum wage or $15 anywhere on the site) and an "Expand housing supply to drive down costs" quote (the housing section only frames housing as unaffordable and a basic human need, with no supply/zoning-specific commitment); the `minimum_wage` and `housing_supply` positions built on those quotes were removed, and the housing priority and healthcare quotes were corrected to text actually on the page. Federal key votes and FEC totals for incumbent Nick Langworthy are added separately by script.
